summary: Frontend verification of the DOM-swap kitchen print fix (replacing prior iframe approach). Ran end-to-end Playwright against the real preview URL with window.print spied via addInitScript to capture DOM state at the exact print-call moment. ALL 8 CRITICAL FLOWS PASSED: (1) Kitchen login cuisine@burgertimes.fr -> /kitchen OK. (2) Two live test orders (BT-B256TD, BT-NCLMH1) created via /api/checkout/session appeared in Nouvelles within polling window. (3) Accept & Imprimer on order1: window.print called exactly 1x, AT print-call moment #kitchen-print-standalone existed in DOM with correct order number + full receipt text ('COMMANDE #BT-B256TD', '1x Cheese', 'TOTAL : 4,00 EUR', 'A EMPORTER'), <html> had 'kt-printing' class, computed #root display='none', computed #kitchen-print-standalone display='block'. (4) After afterprint fired: standalone div removed AND kt-printing class removed — full DOM restore verified. (5) Order transitioned Nouvelles->Acceptées and print badge showed 'En attente d'impression' (expected — no ESC/POS bridge in this env, matches iter16). (6) Réimprimer on Acceptées: same DOM swap+cleanup verified again, spy fired 1x with correct order content; order stayed in Acceptées (status unchanged). (7) Decline order2 with reason 'Rupture stock TEST' -> moved to Refusées and reason visible on card. (8) Regression smoke: /admin/login, /menu, / all 200. ZERO console errors, ZERO page errors throughout entire flow. Cleanup: both orders DELETEd (200) and original hours_per_day restored (200).
critical_code_review_comments: KitchenReceiptPrint.jsx uses a 30s setTimeout fallback that is never cleared even when afterprint fires early — done-flag makes it idempotent but retains closure over the injected div for 30s. Minor memory hygiene; unchanged from iter16 feedback.

Module-level singleton `activeContainer` is fine given the busyIds guard on accept/reprint buttons, but two rapid-fire teardown+append cycles from independent code paths could still race if a future feature triggers print outside the guarded handlers.

Only real remaining risk is device-specific: verification here covers Chromium DOM/CSS semantics — the CSS rule `html.kt-printing #root { display:none !important }` uses plain (non-@media) selectors so it must apply on any browser that supports basic CSS specificity, which is universal. The SUNMI Android WebView-specific bug from iter16 (iframe not isolated) cannot exist with this approach because there is no iframe at all — print rasterizes the visible page and the visible page IS the receipt.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The DOM-swap print approach is verified robust at the CSS/DOM layer using a print() spy that captures a synchronous snapshot of computed styles + DOM at the moment window.print() is called. This is a stronger proof than iter16 (which only counted appendChild/removeChild of the iframe) because it directly asserts (a) receipt is present, (b) #root is display:none, (c) kt-printing class is on <html>, (d) receipt div is display:block — all at the exact print instant. If regression testing this again, reuse the addInitScript window.print override pattern (see /tmp screenshot dir logs) — it works reliably in headless Chromium and doesn't hang on the native print dialog. The only thing that cannot be tested here is the physical SUNMI Bluetooth printer output — that remains a manual user-side verification.
rca of the issue: N/A — fix verified. Root cause per problem statement: Android WebView on the SUNMI tablet does not isolate <iframe> content when window.print() is called at the iframe scope — it rasterizes the visible top-level page instead, so the previous iframe-based fix (iter15/16) actually printed the kitchen dashboard. Main agent's new fix eliminates the iframe entirely and instead uses a plain (non-@media) CSS class 'kt-printing' on <html> that hides #root and shows a receipt div appended to <body>, then waits 2 rAF ticks before window.print() and restores on afterprint (or 30s fallback). Since the receipt is the ONLY visible content in the top-level DOM at print time, WebView-quirky browsers cannot rasterize the wrong thing. Confirmed via spy: computed #root display='none' + standalone display='block' + kt-printing on <html> + correct order text — all present at the microsecond window.print() runs, and all cleaned up afterwards.
